paraphrase: The sentient is of two kinds: untouched by sorrow and touched by sorrow. Ramā (Lakṣmī) is eternally untouched by sorrow; all others are touched by it. Those touched by sorrow are either liberated or still in sorrow; those in sorrow are either fit for liberation or unfit.

paraphrase: The liberated are of five kinds — gods, sages, ancestors, rulers and humans — and so are those fit for liberation. Those unfit for liberation are of two kinds: those going to darkness and those who remain in transmigration. Those fit for darkness are of four kinds — daityas, rākṣasas, piśācas and the lowest of humans — and they are further of two kinds: those who have reached blinding darkness and those still in transmigration.

paraphrase: The insentient is of three kinds by the division of eternal and non-eternal. The Vedas are eternal; the Purāṇas and the like, time and prakṛti are eternal-and-non-eternal; the non-eternal is of two kinds, uncompounded and compounded. The uncompounded are the mahat, the I-principle (aham), buddhi, manas, the ten senses, the (five) subtle elements and the five elements; the compounded is the cosmic egg and all that is within it.

paraphrase: Creation, maintenance, dissolution, control, ignorance, awakening, bondage, release, happiness, sorrow, covering and light — of this whole (dependent reality) these come from Viṣṇu, in brief and in detail.

paraphrase: The knowable is of two kinds, independent and dependent; the independent is the Lord Viṣṇu, free of defects and full of all good qualities. The dependent is positive or negative; negation is threefold (prior, posterior, constant). Mutual non-existence (difference) is not a separate negation, because it is the very nature of positive and negative entities. Positive being is sentient or insentient.

paraphrase: The dependent sentient is either eternally free — Śrī alone — or bound to transmigration, and the latter are liberated or unliberated. Among the liberated, from the lowest up to Brahmā, each class is a hundred times greater than the one before; Ramā exceeds them in all qualities, and Hari is infinitely greater than she. The unliberated are of three kinds — high, middle and low: the high are fit for liberation, the middle ever return (in saṃsāra), the low are fit for eternal darkness.

Qualities, actions, universals and the like are all properties of the thing.

paraphrase: A thing's form (rūpa) is of two kinds: that which lasts as long as the thing, and that which is split off (temporary). With temporary forms there is both difference and identity; with lasting forms there is no difference. This holds between a modification and what is modified, effect and cause, a quality and its possessor, an action and its agent, a universal and the particular, the qualified and the pure, and a part and the whole.

paraphrase: Valid knowledge (pramāṇa) is what accords with its object (yathārtha). It is of two kinds: knowledge itself (kevala) and its means (anupramāṇa). Knowledge itself is of four kinds — the Lord's, Lakṣmī's, the yogins' and the non-yogins' — the first two beginningless and eternal. The means are three: perception (the faultless contact of sense and object), inference (faultless reasoning) and authoritative word (faultless speech). Presumption and comparison are kinds of inference; non-existence is known by inference and by perception.

paraphrase: The purport of all the scriptures cannot be the identity of soul and Supreme Self, since that contradicts every means of knowledge — no one experiences 'I am omniscient, lord of all, without sorrow, without defect', and the contrary is experienced. No scripture teaches non-difference; all teach difference. The teaching 'atat tvam asi' ('you are not that'), given nine times with examples (the bird tied by a string, the honey gathered from many trees, the rivers entering the sea ...), is not a teaching of non-difference.

Yet to delude the asuras and others he sometimes shows sorrow, ignorance and confusion, so that liberation is hard to win (for the unfit); by the fault of seeing him falsely they do not reach liberation and go to darkness. His qualities, actions and the rest are his very nature, so there is no difference among them at any time.

paraphrase: That something is unsublated at all times is known by the witness alone. Time is directly perceived by the witness, even in deep sleep; past and future time too are within its range, and inference cannot reach them. Everything seen or remembered is set in time established by the witness, so without it nothing could be remembered or seen. Hence the reality of what is apprehended without defect is certified by the witness, and by it the reality of examination and the rest.

This real flow of the world has the five differences — of soul and Lord, of souls from one another, of matter and Lord, of material things from one another, and of matter and soul. paraphrase: (The Lord says:) I alone am full of all qualities; my designator is the praṇava, which, from 'a' to 'atiśānta', is eightfold; it designates my forms Viśva, Taijasa, Prājña, Turīya, Ātman, Antarātman, Paramātman and Jñānātman.
speaker: the Lord (as reported by Madhva)

paraphrase: The Lord has fifty further forms, designated by the fifty letters as differentiated from the praṇava — Aja, Ānanda, Indra, Īśa, Ugra, Ūrja, Ṛtambhara and the rest down to the last; from the praṇava arise the eight-syllable Nārāyaṇa mantra, the vyāhṛtis, the twelve-syllable mantra with the Keśava forms as its deities, and the Gāyatrī.
speaker: the Lord (as reported by Madhva)

paraphrase: May Keśava protect me, who grants immortality when worshipped, remembered, meditated on, praised and spoken of. For the peace of this world scorched by the three afflictions, the Kṛṣṇāmṛtamahārṇava is told. Those who have not received Hari's initiation (dīkṣā) nor worshipped Janārdana are beasts among men; what is the fruit of their life?
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: The Ekādaśī of both fortnights is to be fasted; an Ekādaśī touched by the tenth day is to be given up; when the Ekādaśī is overlapped, or with Śravaṇa, the fast is kept on the Dvādaśī (and broken on the Trayodaśī); if the Ekādaśī is not overlapped, the Dvādaśī must not be neglected; for breaking the fast and for death rites the lunar day current at that time is taken.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: One on whose forehead the straight, gentle upright mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) is seen is pure and worthy of honour, even if an outcaste; the face without it is like a cremation ground; sacrifice, gifts, austerity, study and offerings to the ancestors done without it are fruitless; whatever one whose body is marked with gopīcandana looks upon becomes pure.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: Victory to Acyuta, to whom — having laid down all actions in him with an inward-turned mind, without desire and without 'mine' — one goes as the Supreme. Rising while remembering Hari, one purifies oneself as prescribed, cleans the teeth, sips water and bathes according to rule.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: When the dark eighth day falls with the Rohiṇī asterism at midnight it is called Jayantī, destroyer of all sins; since on it Hari, the unborn Lord, was born at midnight, that day is supremely holy, and it is always to be kept by fasting by all — especially by the twice-born and by his devotees.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: I praise the praiseworthy Vāsudeva, ever blissful and stainless, the lord of Indirā, who grants boons even to the first of those who grant boons.

paraphrase: (Quoting a scripture on Bhāgavata 10.87.14:) Two defective prakṛtis abide in each person — one covering the soul's own qualities, the other covering the Supreme; the Supreme Person destroys the first and removes the second, and grants the state of liberation. Both are unborn; the one covering Hari does not cover Viṣṇu but covers the knowledge of him. Śrī, Bhū and Durgā are the (higher) prakṛti called śakti.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: Having expounded the bhāṣya and removed the stain of Kali, he installed at Rūpya (Uḍupi) the immovable image of Kṛṣṇa, carried in play though thirty youths could not move it, and went again to bow to Vyāsa; he crossed the Gaṅgā without a boat, won over the Yavana king by his own words, turned robbers on the road against one another, and at times by yoga became like a rock.

paraphrase: Yoga is the supreme worship (of the Lord) with devotion by a person who does the prescribed acts and avoids the forbidden — 'skill in action'. Hari, independent, abides in me and pervades my limbs; self-governed, the Unborn moves me by his will; the activities of my mind, speech and body are his worship, and I should remember Hari as their doer and their aim. This yoga fully pleases Viṣṇu and grants release from bondage.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya

paraphrase: A father should train his son from childhood in devotion, dharma and vows; the twice-born worships his teacher, keeps pure conduct and daily rites, studies the Veda and Madhva's Mahābhārata-tātparya-nirṇaya and, to still obstacles to knowledge, worships Narasiṃha and Kṛṣṇa. One with beginningless devotion to the Supreme, sinless, trained in grammar and reasoning, learned in the Veda, austere and under vows, gains the supreme knowledge from the teacher's grace. Having heard the Sūtrabhāṣya and other works he reflects on them with companions. The ācārya initiates the prepared devotee, has him sip the Lord's foot-water, and the initiate keeps the vows the teacher gives.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya

paraphrase: When one sits with the body straight the suṣumnā shines, lit above the crown by the sun's rays; in the lotus of the heart one remembers Nārāyaṇa, and before him one's own self as his reflection, praying: 'You are the original (bimba), I am the reflection, though there is a difference between us; flawless Lord, separate my faults from me — homage to you.' So entreated by his servant, he removes the sin.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya

paraphrase: Purity, posture, breath-control, non-possession, non-violence, truth, non-stealing, continence, austerity, contentment, sacrifice and the other duties, study, worship of Hari, fixation, hearing, reflection, meditation, samādhi, exposition of the Upaniṣads and devotion are to be practised, each later one with special weight. If hearing and the like are available the others may be reduced; if one wishes to reduce them further one should renounce; hearing and the rest are never to be reduced; and the vow of Nārāyaṇa's day (Ekādaśī) is to be kept with special care.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya

paraphrase: Hari, present in the image worshipped, is the enjoyer of his own form; present in the offerings — scent, flowers, food, fan, umbrella, music — Viṣṇu accepts himself as present in the image; Viṣṇu within the worshipper and Hari in the image are (the same Lord) in the forms of worshipped and worshipper, enjoyer and enjoyed.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya
